On a turn, players can discard a card, draw from the deck, or draw from an opponent's discard pile. If a player discards an "A" card, everyone has to pass one card to the right. To win, yell "Panda Panda!" when you start a turn with a completed hand. Can you collect the right cards, figure out what your opponents are going for, and time the "A" cards correctly? Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Objective Meet one of the 6 winning conditions to win the game. (See Table in upper right) To win • Cards in your hand must match the winning conditions exactly (cannot have extra cards) • You do not win the round that you achieve the condition. You declare victory the following round. Game Play On your turn, either • Draw a card from deck or from your own or the top card from another player's discard pile • Discard a card Special note about "A" • If you discard an A, everyone pass a card to the player on their left (total number of cards in your hand does not change). • You cannot draw an A from the discard pile Game End All players are dealt 5 cards to restart a new round when 1 player wins a round. The player who first wins 2 rounds wins the game. [Rating: 2/10] Not much here. It is in most cases just going to be a short discarding race of a couple of rounds.

[Rating: 2/10] Played it at GameStorm. One of the most irritating games I’ve ever played. No skill, all luck, and….. well, ugh.

[Rating: 2/10] So cute! Too bad it ends there.  The game has first player advantage for most rounds and that first player can win with a 2 card combo on their second play. The game is very cute it’s too bad it’s broken. Back to the drawing board.

[Rating: 3/10] Winning is basically the just holding something in hand and praying you get passed the card you need or someone does not make you pass. I will tell what I will pass... I will pass on ever playing this game again..ZING!

[Rating: 3/10] This game was okay. I am not opposed to playing it again. I like how colorful the cards are and the gameplay did not feel like a drag, which was nice.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA. I really dislike that you need to get the exact cards (like if it says AAAABBB you need four A cards and three B cards, not four of one kind and three of another kind) and not general patterns for this.  Makes it very challenging to get the precise thing, especially since half the time all you can do is draw a card blind or discard (but sometimes you're allowed to draw from other players discards and sometimes you're forced to pass cards? so strange, and just leads to even more chaos).

[Rating: 4/10] You're just drawing cards and trying to make a set, but sometimes you have to pass a card to an opponent, messing up all of your plans and making it very luck-based.

[Rating: 4/10] ★★☆☆☆ [b]Cute like a panda, but way too light.[/b]  Panda Panda is very light on the rules with only 3 actions to chose from every turn. And the premise of winning the game by holding a handsize-specific card combinations in your hand at the start of your turn is exciting too.  Yet under this cute and eloquent layer of veneer there is no substance. You draw, discard and pass on cards until somebody holds a winning card combination.
